utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are. Good morning, Your Honours. We would call Mr. Nikola Erceg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Erceg.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you. Would you please make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Erceg.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Erceg, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find Mr. Lukic to your left. In a minute he will be standing. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Erceg.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please slowly say your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: My name is Nikola Erceg.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erceg, did you give a statement to members of the Defence team of Mr. Karadzic at one point?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens 1D02360a. I would kindly ask the usher to provide Mr. Erceg with his written statement in hard copy. The Prosecution has already checked the same. We would need first page 6 from this statement since we have to make some slight corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Erceg, would you please open page 6, paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please don't write anything on the statement.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this statement, it says: "The decisions were verified either by the secretary or the person who took the minutes."

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: It should be said "and" rather than "either" because there were two persons doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me read the sentence. It should then read as follows in paragraph 20: [In English] "The decisions were verified by the secretary and the person who took the minutes."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now please the following page. Let us look at paragraph 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can see that a sentence has already been redacted and it is the one that we intended to expunge because the document which is referred to does not correspond. We could not find it in the Karadzic case because the number is wrong.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now we need paragraph 36. Three pages forward in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English version, it's the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The statement reads: "Around 70 municipalities in our region were completely lost." And it should read: [In English] "Around 20 municipalities in our region were completely lost."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please repeat the sentence. The critical word is missing on the transcript because your microphone wasn't activated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. I quote -- the sentence should read: "Around 20 municipalities in our region were completely lost." Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Erceg, now that these corrections have been made, is everything that is recorded in the statement correct when compared to what you told to members of the Defence team of Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, everything else is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is everything that is recorded in the statement truthful and accurate to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you the same questions today, would you provide the same answers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Perhaps I would partly change some things because there are things that I have learned in the meantime, especially when preparing for this trial. Perhaps I might provide more details or more explanations, but on the whole, the substance would remain the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So is there anything else that needs to be corrected in the statement itself?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: No, not in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would tender this statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D982, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D982 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour instructed us yesterday to try to cut down the number of associated exhibits, and I was carefully reading the statement and our opinion is that it would be not possible to understand the statement since this witness actually explained the documents that were mentioned in his statement. The only two documents I found that could be replaced by the already admitted document is 1D02358 which is part of D827, and 1D02826, which is part of the same, D827. So at this moment -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, I hadn't meant to interrupt, and if Mr. Lukic had any additional submissions, I'll sit back down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no additional submissions at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to put our position on the record. We don't have an objection to the associated exhibits. We did -- we do think we identified one additional duplicate. 65 ter 1D02837, we believe is in evidence as P2413. And we invite the Defence to check that before it's tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please verify that, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour, and thank --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think we gave you the option either to reduce the number of associated exhibits or doing that by tendering the documents during the examination-in-chief of the witness so to introduce them through the witness. Now I do understand with these huge numbers that that would not be easy, but that's of course your choice that you uses the statement taken in the Karadzic Defence and, I mean, that's all yours. We'll consider it. But we are not a bit but we are far beyond what is the guidance of the Chamber which you were aware of for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but you know that my last probably ten witnesses had one or none associated exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- but it happens that with some of our witnesses it is not possible to avoid, especially when the statement is taken by another team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it might be a reason to take -- have a statement taken by your own team. We'll leave it for the time being. We'll consider it and we'll let you know as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And although my learned friend already expressed their position, we would tender all associated exhibits into -- offer, actually, all associated exhibits, except those three. So two identified by us and one by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll ask Mr. Registrar to prepare a list so that we'll then decide on the basis of what remains on that list. And could the parties carefully look at whether all the duplicates and whether the documents already in evidence do not appear on that list. Mr. Registrar, I take it that you have sufficient information to prepare such a list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we provisionally reserve the 45 numbers needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibits 983 through to Exhibits D1027, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And these numbers are reserved for associated exhibits related to the statement by Mr. Erceg. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To have the complete record, the Registrar should put the numbers again on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The reserved numbers will be Exhibits D983 through to Exhibits D1027.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's now on the record. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would, with your leave, first read statement summary of this witness and then I will just have a couple of questions as a clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, as you suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At the municipal and regional level, Mr. Nikola Erceg held numerous positions. He was a member of the Municipal Board of the Serbian Democratic Party; a deputy in the Municipal Assembly of Banja Luka; in March 1992, president of the Executive Committee of the Autonomous Region of Krajina; in May 1992, member of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Furthermore, on the republican and federal level, Nikola Erceg performed the duties of a deputy in the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Sarajevo and in the Assembly of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in Belgrade after the first multi-party elections in 1990, then a deputy in the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina after its establishment in October 1991. In the second half of 1992, Mr. Erceg was a minister for industry and energy in the government of Republika Srpska; in September 1992, deputy chairman of the legislative commission of the Assembly of the Republika Srpska; in April 1993, a member of the legislative committee of the Assembly of Republika Srpska again; in May 1993, a member of the board of the National Bank of Republika Srpska. Nikola Erceg worked also as a director of the electricity supply company of Republika Srpska. Before the war, the Serbs' main intention was to remain in a joint state of Yugoslavia with everybody else and all other nations. The ARK Assembly adopted a decision to form an ARK Crisis Staff headed by Brdjanin, and the Crisis Staff became the main body of ARK. After the ARK Crisis Staff was established, the Executive Committee continued with its regular sessions but no longer on a daily basis. Some municipalities demonstrated a high degree of independence from ARK because they were economically strong. The ARK policy was not aimed at a violent or any other form of expulsion or persecution of the non-Serb population, and so the ARK Crisis Staff adopted few decisions and conclusions in that respect. The Banja Luka municipality Assembly, which had Muslims and Croatian representatives, paid attention to the ownership of property, and so properties belonging to those who had left Banja Luka were given for temporary use to Serb refugees. While working as a director of the electricity supply company of Republika Srpska, Nikola Erceg witnessed problems concerning power cuts on a daily basis in households in Banja Luka. He himself did not have electricity in the centre of Banja Luka for 40 days at a time. And that would be the statement summary of Mr. Erceg, and I would just have a couple of questions for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Erceg, would you please now open your statement and look at paragraph 12. It is on page 4 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a second until we can see it on our screens. You say here that the ARK Assembly adopted a decision to form the ARK Crisis Staff. In connection with that, I would show you another document, and it is 1D02309.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: May I do anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a second. Now you can see it on the screen in front of you. That is, the decision on forming the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. We can see that the decision was adopted by the Executive Council and that it is signed at the bottom of the page by Nikola Erceg. Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature. But I know see that in paragraph 12 it should be corrected and instead of "the Assembly," it should be stated "the Executive Council." I have not noticed this until now. And it was the Executive Council that adopted the decision to form the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And before that, did the Assembly also adopt such a decision?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I can't remember, but most probably this was a topic that was discussed. I'm not certain but judging by the obligation to adopt certain decisions, this was something that the Executive Council was obliged to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The names listed here, did you decide that they would be the members of the war staff as it's formulated here or was it somebody else?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: It wasn't me. Mr. Brdjanin brought the list to me. I suppose that it was agreed that he would be the president of the Crisis Staff, and he was also the operative in the sense that he listed the names of people who were to be included in the Crisis Staff. And I was present here in my capacity as the president of the Executive Council which was supposed to verify it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It reads here: "Decision on the formation of the war staff," and we are talking about the Crisis Staff. Is that actually one and the same body?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: No, no. It's not the same body. Perhaps it's a typo. There was no talk of a war staff but it was specifically the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, a typo is when you make a mistake when typing something, but the word appears more than once, which doesn't look very much as a typo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that it was an intention to continue with the error, but I guess that when it was photocopied or reprinted, people who were in charge of that did not pay sufficient attention, and that the sense was changed because there was no discussion of war staffs at the time, nor were they formed anywhere. There were only Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do I understand that you decided that the staff - let me call it "the staff" - would consist of the following people because of it dictated by those who were members of that staff. So Mr. Brdjanin came to you with a list and said, "These are the persons," including himself, and then you say, "Okay, then we'll decide that that's how it is"? Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This list was made on Brdjanin's instructions, but according to the documentation, the staff is made up of people who occupy certain positions, and the very fact that somebody occupies a certain position puts him on the Crisis Staff. I was on the staff because I was president on -- of an Executive Council, and it is written somewhere that presidents of Executive Councils automatically become members of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that true for all 17 members of the Crisis Staff, that they are there because of their positions they held, automatically becoming members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it is not. For instance, some of the members I didn't know until that moment because they didn't occupy any positions. Nenad Stevandic, Mr. Dubocanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I do understand that because Mr. Brdjanin had told you that they should be members and, even not knowing them, that that's the decision you took.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And we just need paragraph 46 from the statement, which is now D982.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, did you tender the document we had just looked at?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This -- this one is, I think, on the list. Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the reserve number for 1D2309 is MFI D993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yeah, maybe I could tender it immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under the reserve number maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under the reserve number. D993, in the absence of any objections, is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erceg, paragraph 46. We see in the sentence before last, two entities are mentioned. When you say there was no communication between two entities, what did you mean by "two entities"?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: What should be written is "between two parts of Republika Srpska." Because it was physically divided into the west and the eastern part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erceg, thank you. That would be all we had for you for the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, let me try to understand in view of paragraph 46. The ... when reading paragraph 46, it appears to me that the lack of communication was especially between Pale and Banja Luka, which is -- I have some difficulties in -- is that well understood or did you mean something else when you referred to the west and the eastern part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A general feature of the first part of 1992 was that because physical communications were broken down between two areas on different sides of the Sava river, there was a division and lack of communication between the western and the eastern part. There was no traffic or communication between the two parts. So in the western part of Republika Srpska, we made do the best we could. That's why the area of Krajina was established and the Crisis Staff, et cetera. So at that time when all communications had broken down, we just made do with our own means and that lasted approximately until the end of June when, as a result of combat operations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're telling me a long story and my question was far more simple. When you said the communications between the east and the west had broken down and when I say -- if I read paragraph 46, it seems that you are there specifically giving an example of the communications between Pale and Banja Luka. Is Pale west or east? Is Banja Luka east or west? Is that included in paragraph 46?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pale is in the eastern part of Republika Srpska. Banja Luka is in the western part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- so when you are now talking about eastern and western part that would divide Pale from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed but I'll first introduce you to the witness. Mr. Erceg, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find Mr. Traldi to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you testified in the Karadzic case; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor in 2001 and 2002, as you mention in your statement. Is it your position that you were telling the truth on all those occasions?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I suppose I was. What I saw as the truth at that time, I said to the Prosecutors. Now whether something will change in my testimony now, I don't know, because I forgot certain things. And some things I will probably put differently, not because I'm changing the facts, but that's the way I see them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you explained similarly in the Karadzic case that you'd forgotten a number of things over the years since you'd been interviewed, as, of course, we all have over the last decade or so, and you testified that as a result what I said -- what you said in the interviews was obviously more accurate. Do you stand by that evidence today?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned during your 92 ter attestation this morning that there might be things that you said differently today than you had in your statement that was tendered because you had learned things in the course of preparing for your testimony in this trial. And I'd just ask if you will agree to, if you are giving an answer based on something that you've only learned in the last year or so or in the course of preparing for your testimony here, specifically tell us that the information you're providing is information you acquired recently. Can we agree to proceed that way?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: We can. I suppose there will be no change in the substance but I may express myself differently on a particular subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the statement that you attested to this morning, that's the same statement you gave to the Karadzic Defence and which was admitted into evidence in that trial, except that the Defence has redacted some references to adjudicated facts and that you made one correction; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now before I move to the substance of your evidence, in your interviews with the Office of the Prosecutor you claimed variously that you didn't know anything about the army, didn't have anything to do with the army, and didn't know how the army organised its affairs. Do you stand by that evidence today?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, then I want to turn to your evidence about the political authorities in the ARK with which you are familiar. Now, your statement repeats assertions that all the communication lines between Pale and the ARK had been severed, and you stated in paragraph 34 that the ARK institutions were formed because of the lack of communications with Pale. In fact, the ARK Crisis Staff was formed pursuant to instructions from Pale; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I suppose that there were some instructions according to which they were established, but I don't know which instructions. I didn't have the opportunity to see that documentation. During the last few days, the lawyers showed me one document according to which the Crisis Staff in our municipality might have been formed, but according to the instructions, there was supposed to be no Crisis Staff of the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, sir --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was in a position to read Djeric's letter addressing this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Erceg, you're moving away from the question so -- the question was focused on the interruption of communications. What Mr. Traldi put to you is that if you say it was formed because there was no communication, Mr. Traldi puts it to you that the very establishment of the Crisis Staff was based on an instruction from Pale which then - and that's implicit in his question - would then have been communicated to you. That's the issue Mr. Traldi is focusing on. Could you please respond to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say this. At the moment the Crisis Staff was formed, I, in that year, 1992, did not see any document saying that a Crisis Staff should be formed. And it was nevertheless formed. Now I can only assume that Brdjanin had that document and on its basis formed the Crisis Staff. At that time, whenever you talked to people, whatever anybody from any institution said, you believed them, and so I believed Mr. Brdjanin when he said there was a need to form the Crisis Staff. I never asked him if there was any document on the basis of which to do it because I didn't need to, and now only I saw during proofing that such a document exists. I saw material documentary evidence instructing the formation of the Crisis Staff, and I also saw in that document that there was supposed to be no Crisis Staff of the Krajina, only of the municipalities. However, a Crisis Staff of the Krajina was formed at the initiative of Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, a document explicitly saying that there was not supposed to be any Crisis Staff of the Krajina, no such document is mentioned in your statement. Can you explain to us what document this purportedly is?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: When I was writing my statement, I was not in a position to ascertain whether such a document exists or what it says. However, during the past few days, I saw that there were perhaps even two documents allowing the formation of the Crisis Staff. One is the instruction of the prime minister, Mr. Djeric; and one document issued by the Main Board of the SDS party I believe in 1991. It's called: Instruction on the organisation and action in emergency situations. This document specifies that Crisis Staffs may be formed in municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, they direct that Crisis Staffs are to be formed in municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, regarding the formation of the ARK Crisis Staff, if we could have 65 ter 32351, page 41, and this will be part of one of your interviews with the Office of the Prosecutor. Now, we see -- and the transcript is in English so I'll read it slowly. We see at the top of the page that the attorney interviewing you says: "In the gazette it was published that you as president of the Executive Council adopted a decision on the formation of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina." Below your initials we see that the interpreter says: "Yes. And below that, that you say: "And that is a verification actually of that which we had received from the central authorities in Pale." And if we scroll down to the bottom of the page, just to be pellucidly clear, the attorney interviewing you says: "So if what you are saying is you received orders from Pale to establish the Crisis Staff in the Autonomous Region of Krajina?" And the interpreter, of course, relays your answer, which is: "Yes." Now do you stand by the truthfulness and accuracy of the portion of your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor that I've just read to you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I do stand by the truthfulness of this part of the interview, but I have to repeat. At that time I didn't know whether documents according to which Crisis Staffs may be formed exist or not, but I allowed for the possibility that some people who wanted to avert a danger were acting on their own in the best faith. In this case, I trusted Mr. Brdjanin when he said that a Crisis Staff should be formed. I didn't ask him to produce a document to show me. If I had held such a document in my hands, telling us that we don't have the right to form a Crisis Staff, I would not have continued. I would not have done that as president of the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: We had to act quickly in that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it right that as of the time you were interviewed in 2002, you understood that what had happened on the 5th of May, 1992, was that you issued a decision forming the ARK Crisis Staff pursuant to instructions from Pale which had been relaid to you by Mr. Brdjanin; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the instructions from Mr. Djeric, which you mention in paragraph 33 of your statement and mentioned this morning, you believe they were received in Banja Luka within two or three of days of when they were issued in late April 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I didn't understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, the Djeric instructions that you refer to in your statement and that you referred to this morning, they were issued on the 26th of April, 1992, and your belief is they were received in Banja Luka within two or three days of when they were issued; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know whether that instruction had reached Banja Luka. I saw it for the first time two or three days ago, so I don't know what the situation was in that beginning of April, but I will repeat, I believed that Brdjanin was acting in good faith when he said we have instructions to form a Crisis Staff. I trusted him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32349, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, this will be part of your sworn testimony in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D407 is what exactly? Is that the Djeric letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, I believe I may have had an exhibit number from the wrong case. I should have said D840, and that's the Djeric instructions according to the list we got from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, you -- because I'm a bit puzzled by the following. Witness, you said you saw that document only three days ago, the document which is referred to as the Djeric letter. Is that ... is that the case? I'm speaking to you. That's difficult for you to know who is speaking to you because the interpreters will translate my words. But the Presiding Judge is addressing you. Is it -- that document, the Djeric letter, did you see it only three days ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was that the document that you was shown to you by the Karadzic Defence as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What then exactly is the document paragraph 33 is referring to? Could -- perhaps, Mr. Lukic, could you assist? I'm talking about paragraph 33. I have been shown document D407. And that would be -- let me just check whether we can -- I find it in the tables. If someone would find it easily on the ... could someone assist me in -- I'm trying to do my utmost best but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, our records indicate that D407 in the Karadzic case, the case for which the statement was taken, is the Djeric instructions to Crisis Staffs dated the 26th of April, the document I'd asked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Witness, apparently in your statement given to the Karadzic Defence, you already commented on that document and you explained certain matters in relation to what is dealt with in that document as well. And that's more than three days ago, isn't it, that you were interviewed in preparation for your Karadzic statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could have talked about that document only because I knew it existed, but considering the whole situation that we knew each other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- witness, let me stop you there. Your statement reads and you attested to your statement as the statement given to the Karadzic Defence, "I have been shown document D407," that means that already far more than three days ago you have seen that document. So I'm puzzled by your evidence where you say, "I only saw it three days ago"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you honestly, I'm not sure about this. I don't know whether I'd seen it in my contacts with the Karadzic Defence. Maybe I saw it somewhere on the screen. But physically, the hard copy, I saw it only when the lawyer, Lukic, showed it to me. Maybe of assistance could be the fact that if there is a connection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you be more cautious when you give answers to questions. If you say, "I only saw it three days ago," where in the Karadzic statement it says already that you have been shown -- of course, I couldn't exclude that it was on the screen or something like that. But that's -- you should be more cautious and more precise in your answers because it's not the first time this morning that we notice that imprecisions are there. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed, but in two minutes we'll take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32349, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's the portion of your sworn testimony in the Karadzic case. Now, here, you're asked: "With respect to this total breakdown of communication that you allege, you also acknowledge in paragraph 4 that in some mysterious way the instructions on establishing Crisis Staff, that is, the Djeric instructions of approximately April 26, somehow made it through this impenetrable barrier, right? You acknowledge that the Djeric instructions were received?" And you answer: "Yes, as far as I can remember I had them, but I'm not sure when. I don't know if it was those first few days when it arrived in Banja Luka. I imagine it was within two or three days." So, first, is your testimony this morning that you never saw the document in any way until your preparation for your Karadzic testimony correct; or is your sworn Karadzic testimony that "as far as I can remember, I had the Djeric instructions" correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question with any degree of certainty. I have now total confusion in my head about this. What I had or didn't have when I was preparing for my Karadzic testimony. I know only that what's in my head now is that I only read this document two or three days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me ask the question very precisely. Do you or do you not stand behind your sworn Karadzic testimony that, as far as you can remember, you had those instructions in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I can take that position. Let it be that way. I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we are at the time for the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are. The witness may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes after the break, Mr. Erceg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom, just briefly one of the remaining issues from the testimony of Vojo Kupresanin. On the 13th of February of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber advising that it had uploaded into e-court the document bearing 65 ter number 31772a, being two pages of Kupresanin's testimony from the Karadzic case, and requesting that, subject to the Defence's agreement, these pages be admitted into evidence as Exhibit P7010. On the same day, the Chamber e-mailed the Defence to see whether it objects to the admission of the document. On the 26th of March, the Chamber instructed the Defence to respond by the end of that day. The Defence responded via e-mail advising that it does not object to the document being admitted as Exhibit P7010, and the Court Officer is hereby instructed to replace P7010 [Realtime transcript read in error "P0710"] with 65 ter number 31772a. And P7010 is hereby admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Erceg, not very polite to continue with administrative matters when you enter the courtroom, apologies for that. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P4337, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: While this comes up, the number should be corrected it's not P0710 but P7010, line 17 of page 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Fluegge. Mr. Traldi, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is the version of the decision on the formation of the Crisis Staff of the ARK that was published in the Official Gazette; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I have three areas of questioning for you about it. The first two are quite brief. First, under the word "decision," in this version it refers to it as a Crisis Staff rather than a war staff; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- could the usher assist the witness in adjusting the microphone so that the interpreters can hear him. Could you please repeat your answer, Witness, because the interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It reads up here: The decision on forming the war staff and then the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then above that it says "war staff." So it's obviously an error. If I have read this correctly. Essentially this is a Crisis Staff. It's no war staff at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We've lost the B/C/S it appears. We have it back now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second question: In the header it says this decision is being taken pursuant to Article 12 of the Law on National Defence. That's the Law on National Defence of the Republika Srpska which by the beginning of May had also been received and was being implemented in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, in fact, it cites the Official Gazette, those were being received in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you testified earlier that the people who were on the Crisis Staff, the documentation said they had to serve on the Crisis Staff as a result of their positions. What documentation were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I do not understand the question. What documents do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. Today you testified that as president of the Executive Council, the documents said that you had to be a member of the Crisis Staff. Let me put it clearly: The documents you were referring to is the Variant A and B instructions; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What document were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: This list of the members of the Crisis Staff is based on the fact that many of the members were -- by the nature of the work that they had to do would automatically be involved in the Crisis Staff. I was the president of the Executive Council, and in that capacity I was co-opted into the Crisis Staff. Just an example. Then Deputy President -- Vice-President Sajic also, then Predrag Radic who was the president of the municipality of Banja Luka, and then Radisav Vukic who was the president of the SDS also by his -- by virtue of his capacity and so on. There is no documentation but judging by the positions these people were on at the moment at which the Crisis Staff was formed, and if documentation is needed, specifically for myself, for example, it could be the Assembly's decision appointing me as the president of the Executive Council. And if you need to find the document, it could be a decision. But in this case, simply, it was by default, automatic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: People who --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to go through all of these people's positions with you in a moment, but before I do, today at temporary transcript page 11, lines 18 through 24, you testified as follows: "This list was made on Brdjanin's instructions, but according to the documentation, the staff is made up of people who occupy certain positions and the very fact that somebody occupies a certain position puts him on the Crisis Staff. I was on the staff because I was president on -- of an Executive Council, and it is written somewhere that presidents of Executive Councils automatically became members of the Crisis Staff." What I'm putting to you now is what you testified then at temporary transcript page 11 was accurate and the place where that is written is in the Variant A and B instructions. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: It could be like that as well. You could interpret it like that. If we need to explain it, it can be interpreted in that way. But it's known --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir -- sir, I'm not at the moment interested in how it could be. Earlier this morning, you testified that you became a member of the Crisis Staff because it was written somewhere that due to your position as president of the Executive Council, you automatically became a member of the Crisis Staff. Just now, you testified there was no such documentation or -- I mean, "it could be the Assembly's decision appointing me as the president of the Executive Council," but that there was no specific documentation saying presidents of Executive Councils became members of Crisis Staffs. What I'm putting to you is: The truth, not how it could be, is what you said the first time, that it was written that the president of the Executive Council automatically became a member of the Crisis Staff. It was written in the Variant A and B instructions, and it was in application of them that you became a member. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: It may be interpreted like that. Let us say that that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, well, we'll not just: "Let's say that it's the truth." You said "it's written somewhere." Mr. Traldi puts to you that it is found in the A and B instructions. Do you agree with that? If not, tell us where it is written.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat again. Specifically for me and my name, I was co-opted in the Crisis Staff for the reason that I was the president of the Executive Council and in some documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you have told us that five times. Now, Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's nothing new for me to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where you said "it's written somewhere," where is it written, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, our lawyers would know that. We received instructions from lawyers how to form a commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you say "it's written somewhere," and if you say "the lawyers told me," then you should have testified: Lawyers told me that it is written somewhere. If you say "it's written somewhere," we expect you to have knowledge of that it is written somewhere. Now, could you tell us where it is written or can't you tell us? Can you or can you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say where it's written. But I know that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Witness, that's an answer to my question. Please, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Earlier this morning you testified that you issued this decision because Brdjanin told you there were instructions to do it and you just took his word for it. A moment ago, you testified that there was a consultation with lawyers about who should be on the Crisis Staff. Was there, in fact, such a consultation, or did you just take Mr. Brdjanin's word for it and issue this instruction?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I did not consult lawyers, but I took Brdjanin's word for it, supposing that he had consulted lawyers, how and in what manner this decision was to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when you testified just now at temporary transcript page 29, line 6: "We received instructions from lawyers how to form a commission," is it your evidence now that that's just an assumption and you don't know whether that's true either?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: An assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As I said, I'm going to go now through the names of the people on this list and their positions with you. If you don't recall or are simply assuming what their position is, I'd ask you to state that clearly. And what I'm interested in is their position before they became members of the Crisis Staff. Now, Mr. Brdjanin, before he became -- before the Crisis Staff was formed, was the vice-president of the ARK Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sajic was the secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that, but I know that he was in the military structures. I don't know specifically what position he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Kupresanin was president of the ARK Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were president of the Executive Council and you mentioned that Radic was president of Banja Luka municipality. Vukic, president of the party. Milanovic --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Milanovic was the deputy president of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And General Talic was the commander of the then-5th Corps of the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Major Jokic was in the JNA air force?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Stojan Zupljanin, head of CSB Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, security services Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Dr. Kuzmanovic, rector of Banja Luka university?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes. But, look, it reads here: "Dragoljub Mirjanic." There is no Kuzmanovic in what I see on the screen in B/C/S. Dr. Dragoljub Mirjanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What was Mirjanic's position?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: He was a university professor as far as I know. He certainly was that. Whether he also had some other position, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Milan Puvacic was the district prosecutor; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: A judge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Jovo Rosic, president of the court?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Slobodan Dubocanin and Nenad Stevandic, they were both with the Serbian Defence Forces or the SOS; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I know that Slobodan Dubocanin was a reserve officer and Nenad Stevandic was a medical student, a student at the faculty of medicine at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First question: What organisation was Dubocanin a reserve officer in? What structure?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know that. I met him around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you hadn't answered directly the question I asked. Aside from the positions that you mention, both of those men were also involved with the Serbian Defence Forces or the SOS; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know this. I -- I cannot answer with either a yes or a no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Djuro Bulic and Nedjelko Kesic, who we see at the bottom, they were both employed by the RS MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Djuro Bulic was in the RS and Nedjelko Kesic in -- what's it called? Security ...I don't know how it was called, but probably attached to the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Head of the -- head of the National Security Service at the CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I think so, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this list includes the leaders of the key institutions in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Crisis Staff provides a forum for them to co-ordinate their organisation's efforts; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, it could be assumed that that was the point, to calm the situation as much as possible and to monitor what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And because of their roles and their expertise coming in, for instance, if something that came up that was a judicial issue, it would be Rosic or Puvacic that took the lead, right, because of their previous positions?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And there were always plenty of people from the various municipalities attending meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Mostly. Especially after the few meetings which were held with a smaller number of people, then later on sometimes there would be as many as 40 or 50 people attending.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm done with this document. And I'd ask for P2413.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this document was ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it needs to be revised as far as translation is concerned, Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We will have it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because it seems that the entry under number 11 is -- the English is not consistent with what we find in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll have it checked, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could you please inform us immediately once you have uploaded a new version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, in paragraphs 72 through 94 of your statement, you discusses relations between the ARK and the municipalities which comprised it, and I'll have several questions about this topic. First, Brdjanin expected that when the ARK Crisis Staff formulated a conclusion, that conclusion would be implemented at the municipal level, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document you discuss in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 2 so just so we've got the text, 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 85 that this was a completely autonomous decision of the Sanski Most Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, one more page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see that this decision relates to the disarmament of what are referred to as paramilitary formations. The reality is that this very order was issued to implement a series of decisions about disarmament made by the Republika Srpska authorities passed down the chain, leading to decisions made by the ARK Crisis Staff, and then passed down the chain to the municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you testified to that same fact in the Karadzic case. So my question is: Why have you not removed the claim that this order was issued "completely autonomously" from your statement, when you know that this, in fact, was an implementation of decisions taken by the higher Bosnian Serb authorities and your assertion about it in your statement is not true?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question from the beginning. Paragraph 82.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Paragraph 85, sir. In paragraph 85 you say this is a completely autonomous decision of the Sanski Most Crisis Staff. My question for you is: Considering that you know that not to be true and you testified in the Karadzic case that this was not completely autonomous but issued pursuant to the decisions by the higher Bosnian Serb authorities, why have you not removed that claim from your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to -- the witness is not looking at the screen, not following the decision. You have the -- that he has the -- this order on the screen. So I'm not sure if he understood the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I haven't. I haven't understood the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you give it another try, Mr. Traldi. And perhaps remove from the screen what the witness has not to look at or even if only temporarily --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it that he should first look at his own statement and if you direct him to the right paragraph that would certainly assist. 85.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm directing your attention your to paragraph 85 of your statement. And you mention that -- the document we just saw in the first sentence. You describe it in the second. In the third sentence you assert this is a completely autonomous decision. My question for you is: The fact is you've left those things in your statement when you know they are not true, and you testified in the Karadzic case, just like you did just now, that the decision we just saw was, in fact, entered into by the Sanski Most Crisis Staff pursuant to decisions by the republic level and regional level Bosnian Serb authorities. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Once again, I do not your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He has to see the document if somebody -- if something is asked about the document. He cannot know by heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's -- Mr. Lukic doesn't have to intervene. The issue is the following. In paragraph 85 of your statement, you are telling us about the document, which is, at this moment, on our screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not on the screen. Let's have a look. Could we now have it on the screen. Yes, but then a B/C/S version as well. Yes. In paragraph 85, you are saying something about an order from the Sanski Most Crisis Staff to the Territorial Defence Staff. That's what you see on your screen now. You see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, you are telling us that it -- this decision was a completely autonomous decision of the Sanski Most Crisis Staff. Now, a few minutes ago, you agreed with Mr. Traldi that this decision was taken pursuant to other decisions taken at a higher level, and, therefore, Mr. Traldi thinks that it's incorrect to say that it was autonomously taken. And he wonders why in your statement you still say that it is a autonomous decision; whereas you agreed a few minutes ago that this decision was taken on the instruction or at least pursuant to decisions taken at a higher level, which would make it not autonomous any further. Do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was in discipline of the lower level which took decisions. It was the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most which took this decision on its own. At this moment, that's how I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But was it taken pursuant to instructions or orders from higher organs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most communicated with, I don't know. I don't think they communicated with anyone at the time when they adopted such a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you testified a moment ago -- I'm just pulling up the specific language. I showed you this decision. I said: "We see that this decision relates to the disarmament of what are referred to as paramilitary formations. The reality is that this very order was issued to implement a series of decisions about disarmament made by the Republika Srpska authorities passed down the chain, leading to decisions made by the ARK Crisis Staff, and then passed down the chain to the municipality; right?" And you said: "Yes." Do you agree with me that are you now changing your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that moment, the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- was not aware [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- the witness should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should you make -- you can make an objection. You should not interpret the -- what's the objection, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First he did not show him the other -- the other documents. He claimed that there were some. Second, the witness did not pay attention to the document in front of him. It was obvious he was watching his statement all the time. We all saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're giving evidence on what happened in court --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I saw it. I can give evidence about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I could follow [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic -- Mr. Lukic, stop now immediately. You say you could give testimony about it. That's exactly what you're not supposed to do in this court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was observing the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, everyone observed it. It is not here --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was not looking at the screen at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you apparently have a very bad understanding of what the rules of procedure requests -- require from you at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm not in a discussion with you. I'm telling you something --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I do understand the proceedings, Your Honour. I cannot accept that I do not understand the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider that with my colleagues. I do it immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's unanimous in this Bench that you did not procedurally properly act, Mr. Lukic. We leave it to that for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you telling me that Mr. Mladic has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- incompetent Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want an answer to that [overlapping speakers] -- so you should replace me then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, now first -- first of all, I'm not in a position that I have to answer your questions. That's one. And second, if you continue to behave like this, we have to consider what to do. I leave to that. And I've now said it five times "I leave it to that," and that implies that you should leave it at this moment as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's it. Mr. Traldi, at least your question, the question also you put earlier to the witness, was a pretty composite one and that may create some of the problems which have arisen now. So even if you would try to find out whether the witness changed his testimony, your previous question should be split up and you should seek confirmation on all elements contained in it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One more thing, Your Honours, if I may. I was just warned because I was following the English channel, my colleague Stojanovic told me. The translation this witness was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Translation issues can always be discussed. Is there any translation issue, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was receiving the translation that on our screens we have decision and here it says "order." I don't know, I wasn't following that channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What line, what word exactly is -- and if you want to consult with Mr. Stojanovic, of course, you can do that. But I'm afraid that these words have been used so many times, that in order to detect any translation error, any interpretation error, we would have to know exactly which line, which page. And the Chamber is, as always, Mr. Lukic, open to a careful review to be very precise ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English it was said "order." So you have "order" in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what, under those circumstances, we would do, we would use the WordWheel and that reveals that the word "order" was used, two, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine times today so choose whatever "order "you would like to have verified and we'll do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But the problem, Mr. Lukic, is that in the statement, the witness is using the term "decision."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly, but on the screen we have the word "order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, you said that already. I just wanted to draw your attention --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- and you see in the WordWheel, we have, I think, 20 or 30 times "decision."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I only dealt with "order" in the singular, not in the plural, because that adds another two.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- in B/C/S it says "order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 85 of the statement of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says it is an order of Crisis Staff of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we see at least in the document itself, the English version, and it's still on our screen, says "order," and is there any problem in relation to the original B/C/S whether "order" could possibly be an incorrect translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In both B/C/S and English versions of the statement it says "order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, I don't know whether this explains all of the confusion because whether decision or order, the issue was not the name of it but the issue was whether this was autonomously taken, yes or no. And, Mr. Traldi, you may resume from there. And, again, one of the previous questions where you asked the witness to confirm, yes or no, was a pretty composite question, so if you would please keep that in mind if you continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you're aware that the ARK Crisis Staff was taking decisions on the disarmament of what it referred to as paramilitary formations shortly before this decision, the 20th of May, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're aware that the Bosnian Serb leadership was taking similar decisions at the same time that were being relayed to the ARK, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're, in fact, aware that this order -- this order was issued in the implementation of those decisions which had been passed down the chain of command from the republic level to the ARK level to Sanski Most; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So last question on this topic. When you say Sanski Most took this decision completely autonomously, what you mean is they were implementing decisions from the ARK which was itself implementing decisions from the leadership; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: After a certain time, after five or six meetings of the Crisis Staff, indiscipline began in the execution of the decisions of the Crisis Staff. It is possibly under that impression that I formulated it this way; that there was a lack of discipline. That's why I said it was a completely autonomous decision. Of course, it wasn't because it follows from the instructions of higher instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to look at a couple of other examples of the relations between the ARK and the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 06929.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a set of conclusions from the ARK Crisis Staff meeting held on the 10th of June, 1992. First, point 1 notes regarding the election of Professor Dragoljub Mirjanic as rector of the University of Banja Luka, the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina only endorsed the recommendation of the outgoing rector, Rajko Kuzmanovic, that the new incumbent be Professor Dragoljub Mirjanic. Now, when we were looking at the list of members of the Crisis Staff, you said you didn't remember if Professor Mirjanic held any position other than that of a professor. Does this document refresh your recollection in that regard?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: To some extent, yes. I should have to compare dates. I don't know which is older, his appointment as rector or his joining the Crisis Staff. This was on the 10th of June so it was after the Crisis Staff was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to point 4, we read: "Only children, women and the elderly may move out voluntarily, that is to say, at their own free will, from the Autonomous Region of Krajina." Now, in paragraph 80 of your statement, you say that the Crisis Staff's position was that if Muslims and Croats wanted to leave the area, they should be allowed to go. This conclusion restricts the Muslims and Croats who are allowed to go to women, children and elderly people. That's because thousands and thousands of non-Serb men were, by this date, 10 June 1992, already been held in camps throughout the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Would you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. You say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Traldi, it's composite to the extent that there two portions in it; the first, who are excluded, and the second, why they were excluded. Those are two separate matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I intended to move as efficiently as possible but I'll split it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, you agree that point 4 here says only children, women and the elderly, meaning, for instance, that Muslim and Croat men who willed to leave the ARK were not being permitted to do so, according to this conclusion by the ARK Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Well, this conclusion is related to the more sensitive group, that's to say, women, children, and the elderly; but otherwise, anyone who wanted to leave could leave. We are just placing the emphasis -- the emphasis is being placed here on the higher risk groups, if we're talking about paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you're aware as you sit there today that, in fact, as of the 10th of June, 1992, there were thousands and thousands -- in fact, more than 10.000 Muslims, mostly men, being held as prisoners in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's break that up. You're aware, of course, that by this point there were camps in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, military camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're aware that those military camps held Muslims and Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're aware they held large numbers of Muslims and Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're aware that the people detained there were mostly men, though not exclusively; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so what I'm putting to you is that those numbers of men, mostly, who you were aware were being detained in camps, that they aren't able to move out what's referred to as voluntarily because they're being detained in camps; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Well, not all Muslims were held in camps. Many Muslims were walking about the streets of towns normally. In Banja Luka included. It's not true that all of them were locked up. There were in the municipal assembly members who were Muslims and Croats, and they continued working normally and participating in the work of the assembly refresh your recollection Assembly of Banja Luka. I'm talking again about Banja Luka because that's what I know best.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P7283, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one additional question to you, Witness. You say children, women, and the elderly were mentioned because they were the most vulnerable group. If that is the case, you would have expected it to read: At least children, women, and the elderly may move out, or certainly children, women, and the elderly may move out. However, the text reads: "Only children, women and the elderly may move out," which is language which you would use if would you exclude other groups. Do you have any comment on the textual interpretation I gave compared to the textual interpretation you gave. Not say that it is mine but I pointed to a certain use of language. So, therefore, the uses of the word "only" which -- how to reconcile that with your interpretation of this paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it fits in the sense that this is firmly regulated, and the assumption was that it would be only women, children, and the elderly wanting to leave, but, in practice, it was different. Others could leave too. Perhaps with a certain delay, pending a process of verification or vetting, who the person was and why they wanted to leave. The very fact that this group was given more liberal treatment in moving out was caused by the fact that there was a lot of -- lot of migration and a great influx of Serbian refugees from other areas. There were cases when Croats organised themselves and wanted to leave and go across the Sava river. There were all sorts of situations that do not fit into any paragraphs. Of course, there were deviations from what we wanted, and there were many things that could not be fitted into any frame or any decision. It was war time. Obviously, a very complex situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put a follow-up question. Mr. Erceg, that was a long explanation. Now I'm talking to you. But you -- earlier you said: "But otherwise anyone who wanted to leave could leave." "Anyone who wanted to leave could leave." This is not in accordance with what you explained now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, look, it all depends on the period. In the beginning, it was perhaps more difficult to leave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I stop you. We are talking about June 1992 and especially about this document, where it says: "Only children, women, and the elderly may move out voluntarily," and then you said, "but otherwise anyone who wanted to leave could leave." Why did you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I cannot focus my observations only on one date, between 1 and 30th June, for instance. I'm talking about the times we lived in. How do I know now what happened on the 8th or on the 10th of June? I'm talking about a longer period of one or two years, and I'm trying to present to you what happened in those situations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But that was not the question. Thank you. Mr. Traldi.
