utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, the Chamber has received evidence that on 26 May 1992, the ARK Crisis Staff determined that its decisions were binding for municipal Crisis Staffs. Now, in your view, when you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor and your recollection was fresher, that was a consequence of the Djeric instructions we discussed earlier; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can we have P3758, page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that. The previous document, the Chamber has not yet decided on it. P7283 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is the book of minutes of the Kljuc Crisis Staff. We see on the 27th of May, one day after the ARK Crisis Staff decision we just discussed, that at point 1, the Kljuc Crisis Staff is concluding that it will give legitimacy to all the decisions of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region. That reflects that it is the very next day implementing the ARK Crisis Staff's decision that municipal Crisis Staffs are essentially obligated to follow its decisions; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning next to Prijedor. It's correct that you can't point to a single document or a single instance where the Prijedor Crisis Staff refused to follow or implement ARK Crisis Staff decisions about, for example, dismissing people from work; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this Chamber has received evidence from a member of the Prijedor Crisis Staff named Bosko Mandic who testified that the Prijedor Crisis Staff implemented decisions by the ARK Crisis Staff. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: In part, yes, they probably carried out the bulk of the decisions but not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in paragraph 82 of your statement, you refer to a decision by the Prijedor Crisis Staff dated the 23rd of June, 1992. Now, the Chamber has received evidence that before this decision was issued, the Prijedor Crisis Staff was implementing ARK decisions by, for instance, introducing a permanent duty rotation. That's P6949. You're aware of that; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Chamber has received evidence that on the same day that the decision you referred to was issued, the Prijedor Crisis Staff forwarded for implementation an ARK Crisis Staff conclusion about dismissing non-Serbs and Serbs who hadn't accepted the SDS as the only representative of the Serb people from important jobs. You're aware of that too; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know these details. I don't know that these things happened. There were individual cases -- I mean, I don't know about any individual cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So is your evidence now that you simply don't know, as you sit there, whether the Prijedor Crisis Staff implemented ARK Crisis Staff decisions or not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I'm -- I have a slight concern about possible confusion. Witness, I read to you one of the answers you just gave. When asked about the implementation of Crisis Staff conclusions about dismissing non-Serbs and Serbs who hadn't accepted the SDS, you said: "I don't know these details. I don't know that these things happened. There were individual cases -- I mean, I don't know about any individual cases." Were you, when you gave this answer, talking about individual cases of persons who should be dismissed; or were you talking about cases where the Prijedor Crisis Staff implemented or did not implement ARK Crisis Staff conclusions? Are you talking about individual cases of persons or cases of implementation of decisions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About individual cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Individual cases of persons being dismissed? Is that what you ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cases of individual persons. I feared that there might have been some confusion there. We'll take a break first, Mr. Traldi. Witness, you may follow the usher. We'll resume in 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, I use the time to deal with one associated exhibit to the statement of Vidoje Blagojevic. On the 23rd and the 24th of March of this year, Witness Blagojevic testified before this Chamber. The witness statement was admitted as D965. In its Rule 92 ter motion for this witness, the Defence had also tendered one associated exhibit bearing Rule 65 ter number 14584. In court, the Defence did not further address this document, and the question of the Chamber is whether this means that the Defence withdraws the tendering of this document. If we could receive an answer, well, let's say, either today or at the latest on Monday -- or tomorrow. Tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have 65 ter 02585.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm turning to another ARK municipality, Kotor Varos, now. This is a declaration or a decision to join the Autonomous District of Krajina. And it says it's proclaimed that the Serbian municipality of Kotor Varos shall be part of the Autonomous District of Krajina. It's dated the 7th of February, 1992. It's correct that from that point, the municipality of Kotor Varos was part of the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And like the other municipalities in the ARK, it implemented the conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff and the ARK government; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 02774.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you say that again? Okay. It's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision by the Executive Committee of Kotor Varos dated the 6th of May, 1992. And we see that it's decided, inter alia, to limit movement of all people except those employed in the regular and reserve police forces between 2200 and 0500 hours the following day. It refers to limit the working hours for catering establishments and businesses, enterprises and other organisations that work in shifts, adjusting their working hours to the regulations of this decision. Now, this was done pursuant to a decision by the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I don't know if there was an ARK decision. But in any case, all the Crisis Staffs of municipalities had both the possibility and the right and the lack of discipline to act in a given moment in an appropriate way according to their own rules. This decision may be relevant only to Kotor Varos, and even if there was an instruction, it could have ignored it and made its own decision regardless of the ARK Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, sir, I think you've gone well beyond my question. I'm going to ask you to focus for the moment on just the provision that movement will be limited between 2200 and 0500 hours and the date of this decision, the 6th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask for P3415.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision by the regional Secretariat for National Defence of the ARK dated the 4th of May, 1992. It says it's pursuant to a decision of the Ministry of National Defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina from the 16th of April, 1992. So, first, we see yet another decision from the republic-level authorities being implemented by the ARK authorities; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: If you had shown me this decision before the Kotor Varos one, I would have told you that it was under this decision that a curfew was imposed in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I won't have more questions about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd tender 65 ter 02585 and 02774.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Mr. Registrar, the numbers would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 02585 will be Exhibit P7284. And 65 ter number 02774 will be Exhibit P7285.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7284 and 7285 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I apologise, I do have one more question -- or one more reference from the last document. I'll just tell you the Chamber has received evidence in P3415 that as of the 4th of May, public institutions and business enterprises in the ARK - this is at point 3 now that we have it back - should start working according to a war-time regime.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And with that in mind, I'm going to ask for 65 ter 17401. Now, this is a decision by the Kalinovik Municipal Assembly in the SAO Herzegovina dated the 11th of May, a few days later. And I see we only have the B/C/S on our screens. I know it's been released, so hopefully we will have it in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And looking at point 1 in this decision, just a few days later, pursuant to the decision of what's referred to as the SAO Herzegovina War Staff, the Executive Committee of the Kalinovik Municipal Assembly is directing that commercial entities and social service providers in Kalinovik municipal area are required to switch immediately to operation in war-time conditions. Now what I'm suggesting to you, sir, what I'm putting to you, is that we see these very similar decisions by the regional authorities in the ARK, the regional authorities in the SAO Herzegovina, issued at very similar times because they're both implementing republic-level instructions. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I suppose that it is so. However, I don't have any written record. I don't have a communication and I don't have the insight that a meeting was held at any point on the basis of which this was all made to be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7286, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7286 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I want to turn to your evidence in your statement about what you describe as conflict between the ARK leadership and the authorities in Pale. Now, you're aware that Karadzic, President Karadzic, went to the ARK Assembly in late February 1992, gave a report, and that assembly voted unanimously, 148 to nothing, to adopt the RS constitution and accept Karadzic's report on the political situation. You're aware of that; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So your evidence about separatists in the ARK and the Banja Luka option, that really refers to a series of events that were over by the end of February 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: There were separatist inclinations throughout the war, that is to say, throughout these three and four years. They are always present, even now in peace time. At any time there are always different opinions and different logic, so, yes, they were present at the time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, in terms of the views of the ARK leadership, let's look first at 65 ter 19104. This will be a page from a publication called "Glas" dated 5th of March, 1992, a few days after Karadzic's visit. Now we see top of the page in the B/C/S and on page 1 in the English an article called: "Krajina government in the offing," and with the subject: "Assembly of the Autonomous Region in Banja Luka." It's dated Banja Luka, 4th of March. The article starts: "From today on, it can be stated with total certainty that in the area of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, the implementation of the constitution and laws of the Republic of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina has begun. This was stated to journalists at a press conference held after the session of the assembly at which there were ten items on the agenda, by the president of the Assembly of AR Krajina, Vojo Kupresanin." Now what Kupresanin said, what he is being referred to as saying there is the truth, that by this point, the 5th of March, it was totally certain that it was the constitution and the laws of the RS that were going to be applied in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: The Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina did not imply any division. This was a time when we were blocked, so this is just an observation of Mr. Vojo Kupresanin. It's given there or perhaps it's a remark of the journalist who understood it in that way. But this reminds me that we -- it seems to suggest that we are working in accordance with the constitution of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. But, no, there was no constitution of the ARK. The constitution was at the level of the republic and this was a period when we were isolated in terms of communications, so we couldn't work together with everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, this was just a few days after Karadzic had visited and the ARK Assembly had voted unanimously to, among other things, accept the RS constitution which is what Kupresanin is talking about there; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Here he talks in his capacity as the president of the Assembly of the ARK, and I repeat, the ARK has no constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you read slowly -- sir --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but there's--

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you read to yourself slowly the first bolded sentence on the left in that main article. And tell me when you've read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Traldi, do we have -- the bold beginning of the article, is that in the translation as well? I'm -- because I see that it starts with "Banja Luka, the 4th of March," and the last thing I read in that further -- the paragraph further down is the word "Vojo Kupresanin." But is the -- is the heading immediately below the -- is that translated as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That I'm not sure, and it may not be. I see that this portion is translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, of course, if we translate 25, 30 lines and not the five first lines that, of course, could distort our understanding of -- Mr. Lukic, could you assist, whether the first seven lines in bold in the original, whether they appear in the declaration?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I'm trying to follow all the documents, and I'm on three at the same time right now, so I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, take your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- didn't hear your question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I'd like to know is whether what we see in the B/C/S first seven lines, directly under the title, whether that appears in the translation or whether it only starts further down with the left column: "Banja Luka, 4th of March."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are right. I don't see this entry part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Perhaps we proceed for the time building, Mr. Traldi, but I think to leave out, even without indicating that it was done, is not what we expect you to do. And I have no idea whether it helps in understanding the article, but I think those seven lines in addition would be a relatively small effort.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll certainly make a request, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To which paragraph did you refer the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The very first paragraph, the first bolded sentence appears to start: "Od danas," "From today."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm just putting to that you it's clear that it's the republican constitution being discussed in that language; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I will tell you again what I have told you already. In the constitution of Republika Srpska, there are no autonomous regions, and there is talk here about the autonomous regions but it was of temporary character. One could probably reason now that what is written here is in the spirit of the constitution of Republika Srpska, but the Autonomous Region of Krajina itself was of temporary character. It was to last as long as the uncertain circumstances lasted. So, in that sense, it's not clear to me what exactly you're asking me. Let me repeat again: In the constitution of Republika Srpska, it is never mentioned that Republika Srpska consists of autonomous regions. At least as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you two very specific questions. First, at this point in its existence, the 5th of March, 1992, it was, in fact, correct that the Autonomous Region of Krajina was acting and making decisions in the spirit of carrying out the RS constitution and other systemic laws; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Laws, but not the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, second, you suggested that the constitution of Republika Srpska doesn't mention autonomous regions. There are rights and obligations of regions --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- included in, for instance, the RS Law on National Defence from the end of February 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. Setting the constitution aside for a moment, you're aware that, for instance, the Law on National Defence, passed just days earlier, does include a decision of the rights and obligations of regionals -- of regions; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to page 2 in the English and the far right of the page in the B/C/S, we see a discussion about the press conference of the chief of the CSB in Banja Luka, Stojan Zupljanin. Now, you discuss the creation of this CSB in paragraph 59 of your statement. About two-thirds of the way down that column in the B/C/S, Zupljanin is referred to as informing journalists that at the last Assembly of the Serbian People in Sarajevo, a decision was adopted to found an Interior Ministry of the Serbian Republic of BH, and in connection with this, he made it clear that there was a plan to found five centres of the National Security Services, including in Banja Luka. Now, as a deputy in the assembly, as a member of the ARK Assembly who took the decision that you mentioned in your statement about creating the CSB, you yourself were personally aware that it was being created pursuant to RS republic-level direction; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 06395. This is a different document or a different exhibit. I'm going to move on while we try and clarify. But I'd tender first 65 ter 19104.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7287, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, if we have -- do not have the complete translation it should be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I apologise, I should have made that clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7287 is marked for identification pending a complete translation of the "Glas" article.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We now have the right document. These are conclusions from the enlarged centre council session held on 6th of April. If we could have page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S. Sorry, page 3 in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see at point 2 that: "In accordance with Article 127 of the Law on Internal Affairs, all Banja Luka Security Services Centre employees found at work on 1 April 1992 shall be placed under the Serbian Republic of BH Ministry of Interior." I've two questions for you about this provision. The first is: We see again the ARK authorities are implementing the laws passed by the republic-level authorities during the period where you suggested there was no communication between the two; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know when the republican laws were adopted. Probably earlier, before the war operations. Before there was a need to establish the ARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second point: It's correct, isn't it, that we see here that the effect of the decision to create the Banja Luka CSB has been to take the authority that had been in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP over Ministry of Interior employees in the ARK and transfer that authority to the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 06395.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7288, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to a very specific communications point, if we can have 65 ter 18494.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a report by the RS MUP dated the 22nd and 23rd of April, 1992. We see it begins with information coming from Banja Luka and, in the third paragraph, refers to information about events in Sanski Most. This is a reflection that as of the 22nd and 23rd of April, 1992, the CSB Banja Luka was passing information to the RS Ministry of Interior; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 02780.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a daily combat report by the 5th Corps to the 2nd Military District. Now the 5th Corps was based in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the 2nd Military District, as of the 1st of May, 1992, not based in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know that, where they were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As president of the Executive Council, if the 2nd Military District had been based in the ARK, you would have been aware of that, wouldn't you.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Can you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. The ARK was an area where you were president of the Executive Council. You had authority. You had to be aware of what was happening. If the 2nd Military District had been based in the area over which you served as president of the Executive Council, you would have known where it was based; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Well, probably, I would probably know. But the location of the army, I really have no idea where they were, what they were. I knew that they were there, but where their command or office was, I didn't know that at all and I wasn't interested in it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you is, what we see here is through the military communications system now information going from the ARK to the headquarters of what was then the JNA organ with responsibility for the area of Bosnia. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know anything about the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can -- can I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's my general answer, so what went through the army, how the army did it, I don't know. I can just assume that they -- that some information arrived through their communication systems for the needs of the civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic wanted to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask my learned friend, last two documents, whether they are on the list or not. Because we could not find last two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll check at the break. I know we've worked with a couple of different drafts and it may that be one or two were omitted and I apologise, of course, that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It goes without saying that we don't have the documents at all so we cannot follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then would you -- I take it that you have some questions after the break as well, Mr. Traldi. If it wouldn't disturb too much your line of questioning, then I would suggest that you move to another subject first. Then during the break inform Mr. Lukic about these documents and check whether they're on your list or not and then perhaps revisit the matter to the extent needed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you just said that your general answer was that you didn't know anything about the army. In fact, in the Karadzic case, you confirmed that you believed your -- well, first, you were aware of the military communications system and you believed that guide-lines from Pale were forwarded using that military communications system. Do you stand by that evidence today?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can we have 65 ter 31667.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir -- as it comes up, sir, in the context of our earlier discussion of Serb autonomous regions and whether they were referred to in the constitution, would it refresh your recollection if I suggested to you that Article 2 of the constitution directly refers to Serb autonomous regions?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Probably so. I don't remember that, this formulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this, what we see here, is a document sent from the ARK Executive Council in Banja Luka to the president of the Municipal Assembly enclosing an order of the commander of the Ministry of National Defence - Territorial Defence Staff - Sarajevo. Now while the signature is, to put it mildly, difficult to read, it's correct that this is a document you reviewed in preparation for your testimony in the Karadzic case and discussed in one of the draft versions of your statement in that case; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: This is something I don't understand at all. There is no signature of mine, my signature is not there. But it seems that it says down there "Nik," I suppose it is Nikola, and probably typed. However, this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're quite sure that you never -- that this isn't your decision, this isn't your enactment, and you never forwarded it to the Banja Luka Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you should be clear. Earlier it was who signed it and now are you using different language. So I can imagine that you would start a question by irrespective of, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually, I'd referred to the difficulty reading the signature but hadn't directly asked about it before. And so I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have noticed a couple of times that the witness, in taking the next step in the line of questioning, sometimes has some problems. He has told us that this is not his signature. He said that he may have been able to read a few letters. Now, if you ask the rest, make that very clear to the witness that you are not talking about the signature anymore, not about -- specifically about the document but about decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- at the moment, I'm specifically suggesting to you that this is an enactment of yours dated the 29th of April, 1992, which relied on an order by the republic-level Ministry of Defence which you had received in Banja Luka. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Now that I have read this, I could sign it right now, so yes. But there are two things here: It's a document which passed through the Executive Council, most probably. It is not my signature, but I now confirm that this is a document from ARK Krajina and that it was forwarded from the ARK, regardless of the fact that the signature is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So what I'm suggesting to you in the context of the last three documents is that we've seen in the police, military, and political authorities by the end of April information flowing between Banja Luka and the -- and the central Bosnian Serb authorities. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes. But to a lesser extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 31667.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7289, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7289 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now once communications between Banja Luka and Pale were open, there were officials going to Pale from Banja Luka or coming to Banja Luka from Pale on a daily basis; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And by late May 1992, for instance, the RS government was receiving requests from the ARK and conducting official visits to the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Whether it was towards the end of May or not, I don't think so. Because it was in end of June that this so-called corridor was liberated so we could have communication and we could travel again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have 65 ter 02491.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now we only have the B/C/S on the screen so far, but you can see these are the minutes of the meeting of the RS government on the 30th of May, 1992. At point 13, you see on the agenda a request of the Autonomous Region of Krajina concerning investments in PTT. So by 30 May 1992, the ARK was able to relay requests to the government that were being discussed at government sessions; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we can have 65 ter 02495.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: These are the minutes of a government meeting on the 3rd of June. Directing your attention to point 12 on page 2 in the B/C/S, we see a reference to a report from the official visit to Foca, SAO Semberija, Majevica, and AP Krajina. Now the reference to AP Krajina is to a visit General Mladic, President Karadzic, and others had with leaders in the ARK in Banja Luka a day earlier on the 2nd of June, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 02491 and 02495.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibits P7290 and P7291, respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7290 and P7291 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 46 of your statement, you refer to a visit by a delegation from Pale to the ARK in mid-July 1992. That delegation attended -- or at least members of that delegation attended a meeting of the ARK Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: General Talic attended the same session?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, at that session on the 17th of July, the ARK Assembly verified the conclusions of the ARK Crisis Staff and War Presidency in their entirety; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know that either. Do you have the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have P3955.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see an extract from the minutes of the session of the ARK Assembly on the 17th of July, 1992. We see it's attended by General Talic, Goran Hadzic, Milan Martic, Minister Subotic, Minister Ostojic, Minister Kalinic, and a General Ninkovic. We see at point 4: Verification of the decisions and conclusions adopted by the Crisis Staff and War Presidency of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Now, first, does that refresh your recollection as to whether verification was discussed at that session of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember the details now. But -- that this verification was needed, it was. It indicates that verification was done three or four months later. The Crisis Staff acted in May, June, and July. It indicates also that there was no normal political work at that time. So you have verification three months later. I cannot remember the details, but if this session was held, if all these people were present, then, of course, the agenda is also true, as we see it, and I believe that all these people listed here did attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you -- you --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I am not sure about myself. I don't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Certainly in the normal course of business would you have attended such a session; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have page 3 in the B/C/S and the bottom of page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see that item 4 reflects that following a debate, all decisions and conclusions adopted by the Crisis Staff and War Presidency of the ARK were verified. Now, in paragraph 45 of your statement, you say the ARK Crisis Staff never passed its decisions to anyone for verification except to the ARK Assembly if it was able to convene. What I'm putting to you is: The truth is the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff and War Presidency were verified by the assembly in their entirety; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Just a moment. What I wrote here in paragraph 45 was from my recollection, and this here is the official position. Now I see that this verification, indeed, was the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, before I leave the topic of relations between the ARK and the central authorities, I want to discuss Mr. Brdjanin for a moment. Now, first, you're aware that Mr. Brdjanin said Muslims and Croats had to leave the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: He said that a hundred times, but I have never seen an official document saying that. That he -- that he talked about that, yes, he did. He did not put it in an official document, though, of any institution that he every belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was whether you are aware that Mr. Brdjanin said that. Whether there's an official document is a totally different question. Are you aware that he said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 26 of your statement that Brdjanin's relations with the SDS were good for a time, but then he left the SDS and formed his own party. Now, your view in 2001, when your recollection was fresher, was that Brdjanin had very good co-operation with the SDS president and the assembly members and that the common goal which they shared brought them together. Do you stand by that evidence today as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin is a very impulsive person. He's very quick in making decisions. And there were a lot of different situations you could run into with him, both in his interactions with individuals and with authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have 65 ter 32352, page 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be part of your 2001 interview with the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Traldi, inform me if my question anticipates one of your next questions, then I'll refrain from insisting to have it answered. Witness, could you tell us when did Mr. Brdjanin establish his own party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't tell you that. I can't even tell you which year. Could have been 1994, I'm not sure. But I know that he did establish his own party, and for a while, for perhaps six months, it was active. I believe it was called the Popular Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could scroll down to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Ms. Sutherland asks you: "Sorry. I can just -- maybe my question was not clear, but a moment ago you said that Brdjanin had a good relationship with politicians at the republic level." You say: "Yes, there's no question about that. He did have a good relations." And she asks you: "With whom in particular?" You answer: "It's a personal question. How can he now say. His co-operation with SDS president, with the assembly members, it was a very good relationship. How close they were, he cannot tell you anything about that, but it was obvious, he could feel it, that there was the common goal that they all shared which brought them all together." Do you stand by that portion of your interview today as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: You mean the last thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I -- what I just read to you.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you referred to the SDS president, of course, you meant Mr. Karadzic; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I'm still puzzled by some of the language in which -- how to understand that, "but it was obvious, he could feel it ..." Is that a bad recorded -- that you could feel it or -- I'm puzzled by the language, especially the person who would have felt something or could have told something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me try and clarify, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could do, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What this answer reflects is that you personally were able to perceive that Brdjanin and Karadzic and assembly members had good relationships and that the common goal that they all shared brought them all together; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Inside four years, anything can happen in communication. Quarrel, love, affection, disaffection. It's such a broad question that I can't give you a direct answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm asking is what your answer in your interview that you just said was truthful and you stood by reflects. What I'm putting to you is that it reflects that you yourself were able to perceive that Brdjanin, Karadzic, the assembly members had good relations and that there was a common goal they shared which brought them together. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know it's a couple of minutes early but I think that, for continuity, it may be a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could you tell us where you are in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I will be much of the remainder of today, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think you have some 45 minutes left, if I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I expect to use most of that but hopefully not all of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Witness, you may follow the usher. We'll take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for the witness, I have one item left, small one, in relation to P6727. On the 8th of September of last year, the Chamber admitted P6727 into evidence but invited the parties to consider whether admission of a smaller portion of this document would be acceptable. This can be found at transcript page 25408. On the 16th of March of this year, the Prosecution informed the Chamber that the parties had agreed that they were going to rely on the full text of P6727, and that it therefore should remain in evidence as such. And the Chamber accepts the agreement between the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you were aware of the strategic objectives of the Bosnian Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you learned of them in May 1992 on -- at or around the time of the 16th Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Could you confirm for me what happened in May? On what grounds could I assert that this was it or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, one of the things that happened in May was that you yourself attended the 16th Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly on the 12th of May, 1992, in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, but now I should see the materials discussed at that session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We're going to go step by step. First, it was your understanding that it was the military's job to implement those strategic objectives; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything about this until I see what written material you are relying on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you confirmed you were aware of the strategic objectives of the Bosnian Serbs less than a page ago. What I'm putting to you now is: You understood that it was the military's job to implement those objectives that you just confirmed you were aware of. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: The first and the principle strategic objective in my opinion was that we remain in the common state of Yugoslavia. We tried everything to achieve that. It couldn't be achieved so we moved on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're well aware when I refer to the strategic objectives I'm referring to six objectives set out by Radovan Karadzic at the 16th Assembly, none of which was explicitly a reference to remaining in Yugoslavia; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Will you tell me what these six objectives are?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Would it refresh your recollection if I suggested that the objectives set out at the 16th Assembly included ethnic separation, included the establishment of a corridor in the Posavina area, included the Drina not being a border between Serb area -- or between different areas, included control of the -- or included the establishment of borders on the Una and Neretva rivers, included the division of Sarajevo, and included access to the sea? Would that refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, you can say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now those are the strategic objectives were aware of; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the ones most relevant to the ARK were the first, the second, and the fourth; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you referring to -- perhaps you should summarise those again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The ones most relevant to the ARK were ethnic separation, the Posavina corridor, and the establishment of a border on the Una river; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: For me personally, the main objective was to achieve communication, for the corridor to be established. The less -- the others are less important, if you're asking me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your understanding was that it was the military's job to implement these various objectives; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in practice, beginning shortly after the 16th Assembly Session, that meant the VRS, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: It meant what?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you agree that it was the military's job to implement these objectives, that means it was the job of the Army of Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: If political means fail, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: By the time the objectives were set forth, conflict had already started, take-overs had already started; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Conflict began even earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So these were objectives not conditionally to be implemented, objectives to be implemented; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were aware at the time they were announced that assembly members -- at least one assembly member from your ARK area understood the strategic objectives to mean that Muslims who'd left areas claimed by the Serbs wouldn't be able to return; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I don't think so. Everybody was supposed to go back to their home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's have P431 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may be confusion here again. Mr. Traldi was not asking you whether that was your opinion, but he asked you whether at least one assembly member from your ARK area understood the strategic objectives to mean that Muslims who'd left areas claimed by the Serbs wouldn't be able to return. So not whether it was your opinion but whether you were aware that at least one of the members from your ARK area did have that opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Are you confirming that you were, in fact, aware that at least one of the members from the ARK understood the strategic objectives to mean Muslims who had left couldn't come back?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: We insisted on reciprocity as far as possible. Failing that, then it should be the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have page 20 in the English and 16 in the B/C/S. Starting at the top of the page in the English and towards the bottom in the B/C/S, Miroslav Vjestica is speaking about Bosanska Krupa. And if we could turn to the next page in the B/C/S. Just a few lines up from the end of the long paragraph, he says: "In pertinent part, on the right bank of the Una river, there are no more Muslims in the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa. All the enclaves that were there, Rapusa, Veliki Vrbovik, Ostroznica, Babic, Muslim Jasenica and Zavir, we have evacuated them so that there will be none there for the duration of war operations. Will they have a place to return to? I think it is unlikely after our president told us the happy news that the right bank of the Una is the border."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, what Mr. Vjestica is saying here is that because of the territorial objective, the fourth objective set out by President Karadzic, the Muslims who have left that area won't be able to come back; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, but it is based on the fact that in the materials in possession of the Muslim and Croat sides is also written that the Serbs who had left areas that they control have no right to come back either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So is it right, then, that you agree that the policy was that Muslims and Croats who left couldn't come back but you assert that Muslims and Croats, their authorities had similar policies about Serbs who had left. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 74 of your statement, you say in pertinent part about people who left that it's clear that everyone had the right to their property even after moving out. Now, you don't really know whether people who left maintained any right to their property, do you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I think that they had documentation which was sufficient at the time stipulating that they can come back and keep their property, especially since it was all recorded in land registers that had not been tampered with during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph 74 you referred to, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. Though I grant that my notes appear to have been in error on that as -- and I appreciate the correction, Your Honour. I will look for a correct reference, but in the meantime, I do want to call up one page of the witness's Karadzic testimony. And that's 65 ter 32348, page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, I'd like to briefly deal with a procedural matter. The Chamber received information from the Victims and Witness Section that the witness very much would like to travel back tomorrow and therefore would prefer to continue today so as to conclude his testimony. We know that you would need most of this session, Mr. Traldi. I don't know how much time Mr. Lukic would need. What I do know is that due to commitments elsewhere, that I'm unable to continue any longer than 2.30. Therefore, Mr. Lukic, it's to some extent also in your hands, depending on how much time you would need. Could you give us any indication so that we could inform the witness about what he could expect?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I can see, I have at least one session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, we are aware that you asked whether we could conclude today. It's almost for certain that we will not be able to do that. Therefore, unfortunately, but inevitable, we would continue to hear your evidence tomorrow morning, and we regret that we can't meet your request. But at the same time, you'll under that it would be unfair to the Defence not to give them time for re-examination, and they need more time than we could deal with today. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have, please, page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may, before we continue, I'm sorry. This is nothing related to the question of Mr. Traldi not posed yet. I think that there is a flight tomorrow evening so maybe the witness could inquire, since I cannot communicate with him, with the Victims and Witness Unit. So maybe that flight to be organised for tomorrow evening, if he has to leave tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that VWU will carefully listen in to our conversations and that they are therefore alerted to it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think that both VWS and the witness would appreciate your intervention. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, regarding what you just testified about, your suggestion that people kept the right to their property, in your Karadzic testimony, beginning at line 13, you were asked: "Now, in fact, Mr. Erceg, you don't really know much about this at all and you don't know, really, whether people had the right to their property or not. And you even acknowledged that in your own statement at a later portion. That's the case, isn't it? You don't know much about this issue and you admitted it in your statement at paragraph 85?" Now --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know much, that's true, but I know that the land register is -- has greater legal force in all matters of property. So anyone who came back should not have any problems retaking their property.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when you agreed in the Karadzic case that you didn't know very much about this issue, your position now is that you do know things about this issue; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know enough. I know that there are land registers. I know that there are records issued by municipalities and various organs. Who received what kind of paper, I cannot tell you with any degree of certainty what the real truth is. My answer can be both what I said in Karadzic and the one I gave you here. We are talking about nuances of meaning, and I'm not a lawyer. You should not lend greater importance to the form that I answer in. I have no legal expertise, and I cannot find my way around those details in which the date sometimes means to me more than the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: That's why it's difficult for me to communicate with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you now a couple of fairly simple questions and I'd encourage you to start the form of your answer with a yes or a no. The first is: Of these people who were leave, the majority were -- the overwhelming majority were Muslims or Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were aware that there were forced expulsions of Muslims and Croats from the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes. But please, not forced, judging by the records provided by any institution, but one neighbour would expel another for God knows which reasons. I'm just stating that as an example.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, going back to the 16th Assembly Session we were discussing a moment ago, the president of your Crisis Staff, Mr. Brdjanin, endorsed liquidating key Muslims at that session; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P431 back, please. I'll be looking for page 17 in the English and 14 in the B/C/S. Now -- and we have 17 only in the B/C/S, it appears. We're looking for 17 in the English; 14 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We still haven't gotten 14 in the B/C/S. Now we have again two times 17 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, let me put to you the evidence the Chamber has received. The Chamber has received evidence that at this session, Dragan Kalinic said in pertinent part: "Among all the issues this assembly should decide on, the most important one is this: Have we chosen the option of war or the option of negotiating." You can see it now in the second paragraph of his remarks. He says: "I say this with a reason. I must instantly add that knowing who our enemy is, how perfidious they are, how they cannot be trusted until they are physically, militarily destroyed and crushed, which, of course, implies eliminating and liquidating their key people, I do not hesitate in selecting the first option, the option of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now if we could turn to page 24 in the English and 20 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you can see in the middle of your screen Mr. Brdjanin speak, and in the beginning of his remarks he says: "I would like to say a heart-felt bravo to Mr. Kalinic" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we have the right page in English on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We don't. Again, for efficiency, I'll just put the evidence to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Chamber has received evidence that at this same session,

utterances.speaker: MR. BRDJANIN SAID
utterances.text: "I'd like to say a heart-felt bravo to Mr. Kalinic. In all my appearances in this joint assembly, it has never crossed my mind that, although he seems quiet while I seem hawkish, his opinions are the closest to mine." So Brdjanin is endorsing Kalinic's remarks; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: That's why there is a written record, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at the time he is speaking as the president of the Crisis Staff, the highest authority in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, if it was the relevant period. I haven't seen the dates up on the top but probably it is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, in paragraph 91 of your statement, you state you were present at ARK Crisis Staff meetings when Omarska and Keraterm were mentioned. Now, as a result, when you say in paragraph 89, that: "Remand prisons and camps were never discussed at the Crisis Staff meetings," that's not the truth, is it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Well, I think that there were few discussions of -- about these issues. I attended a few meetings of the Crisis Staffs because I had obligations in the Federal Assembly in Belgrade, too, and I was often absent. Whether it was discussed or not, I don't know, but I didn't hear this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In that same paragraph, 89, you discuss your visit to Trnopolje. That visit was at the end of August 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was in late August. I don't know exactly, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as far as you remember, Trnopolje was run by the army; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That means the VRS?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska; yes?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, on your visit you didn't speak to any detainees at all; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I didn't. I wanted to play a role. I wanted to claim that I did not speak Serbian, that I was a foreigner, and that I wanted to hear what went on there. And I was surprised that the situation was relaxed, at least on the day when we were there. I could see that there was a makeshift hospital and first aid and so on and so forth. So I could see that the situation was not tense in any way. And to be honest, I was surprised by this. I heard some issues which are not for this Court which confirmed that it was not a drastic and difficult situation. Whether it was like that only on that specific day or otherwise too, no, I wouldn't really go into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the Chamber has received evidence that international monitors who visited around the same time found detainees living in terror, found food deficiencies, and suggested they should all be released. Did you not notice when you visited that the inmates were living in terror and that there were food shortages?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: There's no doubt about that, if it's a prison behind a wire, that there was terror, yes. But they convinced me that in terms of food and other necessities, that everything was available in adequate supplies. Because I could see that there was an ambulance there, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you refer in paragraph 48 to a meeting that you attended, and you refer to it by its Karadzic exhibit number. But that meeting was shortly after your visit to Trnopolje; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Paragraph 48 deals with the visit of Finance Minister Petra Markovic, who came to visit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Or at least in the version that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have P3880.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I seek clarification of one of your previous answers. You said: "Whether it was like that only on that specific day or otherwise too, no, I wouldn't really go into that." Is it your evidence that you don't know whether it was on the other days the same, or is it that you do know but you think it better not to address it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the situation was like. I only visited Trnopolje once, and also only visited Manjaca once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the witness saying that he doesn't know in more general terms, of course, you could -- you could consider that the Chamber would rely on other evidence where the witness cannot provide any additional information about the other days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, and I would, Mr. President, but I do want to take the witness to this meeting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not keeping you from that, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a document from the 1st Krajina Corps command, 2nd of September, 1992. This is the document that, though under a different number, is described in that paragraph of your statement. Now, in the first paragraph we see a reference to the attendees. It includes an ICRC representative. It includes, on our side, Dragan Kalinic, Mr. Nikola Erceg, Mr. Predrag Radic, Stojan Zupljanin, and Colonel Milutin Vukelic on behalf of the 1st Krajina Corps command. So it's correct that very shortly after the meeting that -- or after your visit to Trnopolje, you had a meeting with the Red Cross. And it says here the meeting addressed all the general issues linked with the London Conference documents that refer to the unconditional closure of all prisoner of war camps. So you had a meeting with the Red Cross about the camps just after your visit to Trnopolje; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes, well, I suppose so. I cannot really judge that now because I don't see the dates. This is the 2nd of September. Yes, I think it was soon thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And by this time, the terrible criminal conditions in the Bosnian Serb-run detention facilities were widely and publicly known; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: It was known thanks to the media, which described many things from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, the Red Cross who you met with had also been publicly decrying the conditions in those camps for a month or more at the time you met with them. You must have become aware of that either during the meeting or during your preparations for it, mustn't you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: It is quite logical that every camp has to be criticised and that there are many objections to any sort of camp. As long as it's a camp, it's out of bounds of everything that is normal and humane, so I am aware that there was a need to criticise this in every possible way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I just want to look at some of the ICRC's public criticisms briefly with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 10866. This is a statement by Cornelio Sommaruga, president of the ICRC, dated the 29th of July. And if we turn to page 2 in both languages, in the middle of the fourth paragraph we refer to allegations of the terrible ravages of ethnic cleansing, in whose name whole populations are being terrorised, minorities intimidated and harassed, civilians interned on a massive scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were aware -- you were made aware during your meeting with the Red Cross that they understood civilians to be being interned in the ARK on a massive scale by the Bosnian Serb authorities; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were all civilians. I'm not so sure about that. I suppose that there were civilians too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not asking for the moment whether all the people in detention were civilians. What I'm putting to you was: You were made aware, during the meeting or before it, of the detention of massive numbers of civilians in the ARK as reflected here; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: I learned that at this meeting. I hadn't known it previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we see 65 ter 10867. Again, this is a press release from the Red Cross. In the first paragraph it discusses visits its delegates have conducted to places of detention in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It says it is evident to the ICRC that innocent civilians are being arrested and subjected to inhumane treatment. And that, moreover, the detention of such persons is part of a policy of forced population transfers carried out on a massive scale and marked by the systematic use of brutality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's also information you learned at this meeting, if you hadn't known it before; right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA ERCEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender 65 ter 10866 and 10867 [Realtime transcript read in error "10876"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10866 receives number Exhibit P7292. And document 10876 -- 10867 -- it's wrongly noted in the transcript. So document -- I'll repeat from the beginning. 10866 receives number P7292. And document 10867 receives number P7293, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7292 and P7293 are admitted into evidence. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I see the time. I have, I would say, about ten minutes of questions remaining and I'm in the Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps -- Mr. Lukic, I received a message from VWS that they would be willing to organise the return journey for the witness, but then -- for tomorrow, but then he would have to leave by 11.30 at its latest. Now if Mr. Traldi would take ten minutes tomorrow morning, if we would start at 9.30 that would bring us -- you would then have some, let's say, 45 minutes left in the first session, and then in the second session, until that point in time you would have a little bit over half an hour. That would make all together one hour and 15 minutes. Would that be sufficient? Because I really need a commitment by the parties to ask VWS to make those travel arrangements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll do our best to allow this witness to leave tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand this as a kind of a commitment that every one does its utmost best. We'll try hard, Witness, to conclude your evidence tomorrow in such a way that you'll be able to travel back. We'll do our utmost best. This is not a guarantee. Apart from that, I take it that, together with VWS, that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Together with VWS, that you will arrange everything in such a way that you could immediately leave from here to the airport, if need be. Before I -- before we adjourn, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony already given, or whether that is testimony still to be given tomorrow. If that is clear to you, you may follow the usher, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 2nd of April, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of April, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.17 p.m.,
